science.qualification: Photosphere color from a blackbody at the star's published temperature, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,675 K and log g 4.24 (u1 0.478, u2 0.248): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Sector 38
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 1.43 days, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 38 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 5.7%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.53%, the light's own noise being 0.15%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 1.42 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.76, a width of 0.48 and a fit of 1.00, and in all 5 of the star's sectors together a period of 1.43 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.72, a width of 0.48 and a fit of 1.00; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random. Gaia DR3 lists 31 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 2.3% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 38

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffefe7, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 102 (March and April 2026): the map's scale, 92% to 108% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 11.4% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · March and April 2026
